name: Joint Pose Optimization

# Joint Pose Optimization

Also called: BARF, Unposed images methods

## Overview
Joint Pose Optimization (JPO) refers to methods that simultaneously optimize camera poses and the scene representation (neural or geometric) to eliminate the dependency on pre-computed, external Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines [S1]. It solves the problem of novel-view synthesis and 3D reconstruction from unposed image collections where camera parameters are unknown or unreliable [S1]. Unlike sibling methods that may rely on incremental depth priors or temporal continuity, JPO typically treats pose and scene as coupled variables optimized via differentiable rendering [S1].

## Shared principles
The methods in this family share the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1][S2, unofficial]. All variants rely on differentiable rendering to compute gradients from the rendered image to the Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)) and/or network weights [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md]. The rendering process remains differentiable with respect to the scene representation [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md]. Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].

## Subtopics

### [1D Signal Alignment for Joint Optimization Analysis](8423-1d-signal-alignment-for-joint-optimization-analysis.md)
A simplified analytical framework used to study the convergence behavior of joint camera pose and scene reconstruction optimization. It reduces the complex 3D joint optimization problem into a [1D signal alignment](#8423-1d-signal-alignment-for-joint-optimization-analysis.md) task to analyze how the signal spectrum affects the gradient landscape. Unlike the full 3D method, this approach isolates the "local phenomenon" of joint alignment, revealing that high-frequency signals cause gradient noise and local optima, which can be mitigated by Gaussian filtering.

## Background
Joint Pose Optimization emerged as a response to the limitations of traditional pipelines that depend on off-the-shelf pose estimation methods, which increase inference time and fail in texture-less regions or when images lack overlap [S1]. Early works proposed jointly optimizing camera poses and neural representations for both static [HJS∗ 23, WWX∗ 21, CL23a, LMTL21, SCW∗ 25] and dynamic settings [LGM∗ 23] [S1]. However, these initial methods required rough pose initialization and were limited to small motions [S1]. Alternative solutions followed incremental approaches, leveraging mono-depth priors [BWL∗ 23] or temporal continuity [FLK∗ 24] to optimize camera parameters [S1]. More recent extensions have enabled generalizable representations [CL23b, HJS∗ 23, XLC∗ 25] for joint pose prediction from sparse collections [S1]. Notably, Ye et al. [YLX∗ 25] demonstrated efficient pose estimation and novel-view synthesis from unposed images using only [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md), though this remains limited to static scenes [S1].
